name: browser viewer spike (Three.js GaussianSplats3D 0.4.7)

GPU time via EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 at 1024x768, 58/60 valid samples: median 2.85ms (351fps), mean 5.32ms (188fps), p95 31.1ms (32fps), worst 37.4ms (27fps) - note the VARIANCE, typical frames are cheap but spikes dip to ~30fps. Caveat: GPU raster time only; depth sort runs async in a worker and is not included. JS-clock timing was invalid (performance.now clamped to 0.1ms, gl.finish non-blocking) - use timer queries, not Date/performance deltas

name: 3DGS drjohnson (indoor) cap1M 15k steps
notes: PASS T1: PSNR 27.17 / SSIM 0.871 / LPIPS 0.289 - BUT these are the step-6999 eval; gsplat eval_steps default [7000,30000] so with max_steps=15000 the FINAL model was never evaluated (set eval_steps explicitly next time). Wall clock 1674s (28min) at 8.7 it/s vs 16.4 it/s for 250k. num_GS pegged at 1M cap. Peak GPU 3883 MiB incl 1678 baseline => 3DGS ~2.2GB of ~4.5GB usable. Final ply 226MB. Indoor beats outdoor by ~5dB PSNR (22.31 south-building) - indoor dense coverage with no foliage suits 3DGS

name: browser viewer @1M splats - VIEWER IS THE BOTTLENECK
notes: 994153 splats load in 12.3s (226MB). GPU time: median 8.2ms (122fps), mean 22.4ms (45fps), p95 127.5ms (8fps), worst 140.5ms (7fps). vs 250k: median 2.85ms/351fps, p95 31.1ms/32fps. KEY M1 CONCLUSION: 6GB VRAM is NOT the binding constraint (1M gaussians trains in 3.9GB peak); the BROWSER is - p95 collapses from 32fps to 8fps at 4x splats, which is visible stutter. M5 needs LOD/compression or a lower cap; a 400-500k sweet spot is the likely product setting. Caveat: GPU raster only, async sort excluded, and camera was re-sorting every frame

name: scene scale + up-axis conventions
source: analysis of exported ply + COLMAP poses
notes: Cost ~1h of debugging - record for M5 viewer. (1) Scene up-axis is +Z (COLMAP convention), NOT -Y; guessing -Y put the camera sideways. (2) min/max bounds of the splat cloud are 33 units but 5th-95th percentile content is only 1.23 units - outlier splats inflate the bbox ~27x, so auto-framing MUST use percentiles not min/max or the camera lands 30x too far and everything is sub-pixel. (3) mean splat size exp(scale)=0.0036 units. (4) gsplat .ply IS standard INRIA log/logit convention - verified, no conversion needed for browser viewers
